title: Chinese EV import quota: current administration
fact: For the second period of quota year 1, from 1 September 2026 to 28 February 2027, the available quantity is 24,500 vehicles plus unused volume from the first period; the quota remains first-come, first-served until further notice.
interp: The current operating rules are more specific than the April consultation. The annual first-year quota remains 49,000 vehicles while administration is divided into periods.
limit: This describes quota administration, not utilization, price effects, investment effects or future allocation policy.
source: Global Affairs Canada - Notice to Importers No. 1168
passage: The quota is administered on a first-come, first-served basis. The total available quantity for the 2nd Period of Quota Year 1 (September 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027) will be 24,500 vehicles plus any unused volumes from the 1st Period.

title: Chinese EV quota: initial implementation and consultation
fact: The first-year annual quota was set at 49,000 vehicles and initially implemented on 1 March 2026 on a first-come, first-served basis for six months.
interp: This establishes the initial quota context, but not the operating rules after 1 September 2026.
limit: Use EV-CC-01 for the later second-period administration rules.
passage: The quota volume for the first year is 49,000 vehicles. The quota was implemented on March 1, 2026, on a first-come, first-served basis for an initial period of 6 months.

title: Section 301 strategic tariff modifications
fact: USTR finalized additional or increased Section 301 duties on selected strategic Chinese products in September 2024.
interp: The U.S. instrument differs in legal authority and product coverage from Canada's EV quota.
limit: Current combined duty treatment requires product-level tariff verification.
source: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative
passage: The U.S. Trade Representative determined to impose additional Section 301 duties or increase the rate of existing Section 301 duties on certain products of China in strategic sectors.

title: Integrated automotive production
fact: More than 90% of Canadian-made vehicles and 60% of Canadian-made auto parts were reported as exported to the United States.
interp: U.S. market access and integrated production remain important context for Canadian automotive choices.
limit: This is trade/production context, not an instrument equivalent to the Canada-China quota or U.S.-China tariff action.
passage: More than 90% of Canadian-made vehicles and 60% of Canadian-made auto parts are exported to the United States.

title: Agricultural tariff changes
fact: China suspended selected tariffs through the end of 2026 and reduced the combined applied tariff on Canadian canola seed to 14.9%.
interp: The measures partially restored market access after the 2025 deterioration.
limit: The announcement does not establish realized shipment or producer-income effects.
passage: Effective March 1, 2026, China suspended specified tariffs and reduced tariffs on Canadian canola seed to a combined applied tariff rate of 14.9%.

title: 2025 bilateral energy trade
fact: In 2025 Canada exported C$157.5 billion and imported C$34.4 billion in specified hydrocarbons with the United States; the U.S. accounted for 90.8% of Canadian hydrocarbon export volume.
interp: Infrastructure and geography give the U.S. relationship structural importance for Canadian energy choices.
limit: The values cover specified hydrocarbons, not all energy.
passage: Exports of crude oil, RPPs, natural gas, and NGLs to the U.S. totaled $157.5 billion for the Canadian economy in 2025.

passage: The roadmap records cooperation and exchanges in energy-related areas.

title: Border fentanyl seizure context
fact: Between September 2025 and August 2026, U.S. CBP attributed 4.85 lb of fentanyl seizures to the Northern Border and 10,216 lb to the Southern Border; Northern Border seizures were approximately 0.1% of the cited border-enforcement total.
interp: The statistic provides enforcement-seizure context for the Canada-U.S. border.
limit: This is a share of recorded seizures, not an estimate of the share of trafficking, production origin, or policy effectiveness.
passage: Northern Border seizures accounted for approximately 0.1% of total U.S. fentanyl seizures by U.S. border enforcement between September 2025 and August 2026. U.S. data shows 4.85 lbs were seized at its Northern Border, compared to 10,216 lbs seized at its Southern Border.

title: Fentanyl precursor supply-chain assessment
fact: DEA's 2025 assessment describes Mexican cartels producing fentanyl using precursor chemicals and pill presses sourced from companies in China.

limit: The assessment is not a complete measure of every trafficking route.
